game.description: A custom deck of 8 cards is shuffled: 1 card worth 2, 2 cards worth 9, 4 cards worth 13, 1 card worth 14. 2 cards are dealt face down, without replacement.
game.contract: The contract settles at the smallest of the dealt cards.

info.raw:
I worked out the probability of each settlement value, then picked the bid and ask that give the best expected profit against both trader types.

**Settlement distribution.** The contract settles at the smaller of 2 cards drawn from {2, 9, 9, 13, 13, 13, 13, 14}. There are 28 possible pairs.

| Minimum card | Pairs | Probability |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 7 | 0.25 |
| 9 | 11 | about 0.39 |
| 13 | 10 | about 0.36 |

The expected value is 243/28, about 8.68. A minimum of 14 is impossible because there is only one 14.

**Ask.** Any ask below 13 is hit by the informed trader whenever the value is 13, which costs money. An ask of 13 never loses to the informed trader. Noise traders still buy there about 25% of the time, at about 4.3 above fair value. The expected profit is roughly 0.85 per quote.

**Bid.** The informed trader only sells below 9 when the value is 2. A bid of about 3 balances that loss against the noise traders' willingness to sell:
- Noise traders sell about 18% of the time, at about 5.7 below fair value.
- The informed trader sells only when the value is 2, losing me 1 per unit.
- The expected profit is roughly 0.79 per quote.

{"bid": 3.0, "ask": 13.0}

The settlement value has three possible outcomes: 2, 9 or 13.

**Settlement distribution (min of 2 cards from 8, 28 equally likely pairs):**
- Minimum is 2: 7 of 28 pairs (any pair containing the 2).
- Minimum is 9: 11 of 28 pairs.
- Minimum is 13: 10 of 28 pairs.
- Fair value = (2·7 + 9·11 + 13·10) / 28 = 243/28 ≈ **8.68**.

**What the first trade tells us:**
- Someone bought at 13.
- An informed trader would never buy at 13, because the value cannot exceed 13.
- So the buy came from a noise trader, and it was equally likely whatever the true value is.
- Fair value therefore stays at about 8.68.

**Ask:**
- Any ask below 13 loses to an informed buyer when the value is 13.
- At 13 or above, informed traders never buy, so only noise traders trade.
- Expected profit from noise buyers is about 0.85 per quote at asks from 13 to 13.5, and it peaks around 13.3–13.5.

**Bid:**
- Any bid above 2 loses to an informed seller when the value is 2. That happens with probability 0.05 per quote.
- Expected profit after that loss is about 0.79 at a bid of 3, and slightly lower at 2 or 4.

I'm short 1, but I'm maximising expected profit and the position limit is not binding, so I'm not adjusting for inventory.

{"bid": 3, "ask": 13.4}

Card 1 is 13, so the contract settles at 2, 9 or 13, depending on card 2. My fair value is about 8.94, and I'm quoting 3 / 13.5 around it.

**Remaining cards.** Seven cards are left: one 2, two 9s, three 13s and one 14. Since the contract pays the smaller card, card 2 decides it:
- Card 2 = 2 (1 of 7): settles at 2.
- Card 2 = 9 (2 of 7): settles at 9.
- Card 2 = 13 or 14 (4 of 7): settles at 13.

**What the history tells me.**
- The buy at 13 carries no information. The settlement can never exceed 13, so an informed trader would not buy there.
- The sell at 3 does carry information. An informed trader sells at 3 only if the settlement is 2. A noise trader would have sold at 3 with probability about 0.18, since the fair value then was about 8.68.
- So a sell at 3 was about 2.4 times as likely if the settlement is 2 as otherwise. I raise the weight on 2 by that factor.

**Updated probabilities.**

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 2 | 0.28 |
| 9 | 0.24 |
| 13 | 0.48 |

That gives a fair value of about 8.94.

**Ask.** An informed buyer can only hurt me when the settlement is 13. Any ask at 13 or above avoids that loss entirely. Expected profit from noise buyers is flat at about 0.85 between 13 and 14, peaking near 13.5.

**Bid.** Informed sellers only hurt me when the settlement is 2. Expected profit is highest around a bid of 3, about 0.77 after the informed-seller loss. A bid of 2 or 2.5 gives roughly the same.

{"bid": 3, "ask": 13.5}

Card 1 is 13, so the contract settles at min(13, card 2). The 7 cards left are one 2, two 9s, three 13s and one 14. That gives these settlement values:

- 2 with probability 1/7
- 9 with probability 2/7
- 13 with probability 4/7 (a 13 or the 14 both give 13)

The public fair value is therefore about 72/7 ≈ 10.3. Quote 3 passing with no trade barely moves this. It only slightly lowers the chance that card 2 is the 2, because an informed trader holding a 2 would have sold at 3.

For each side I compared the expected gain from noise traders against the expected loss to informed traders.

**Ask:** An informed trader never pays more than 13.
- Profit from noise buyers keeps rising up to about 15. Expected value is about 0.83 at 14, 0.86 at 15 and 0.83 at 16.
- The best ask is about 15.

**Bid:** An informed trader sells only if the value is below my bid. With a bid under 9, that only happens when the value is 2.
- Expected value is about 0.74 at a bid of 4, 0.76 at 5 and 0.74 at 6.
- The best bid is about 5.

{"bid": 5, "ask": 15}

game.title: Dice/cards max
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (4 faces, each equally likely): 2, 4, 8, 8.
- Die 2 (4 faces, each equally likely): 4, 6, 7, 12.
- Die 3 (6 faces, loaded): 0 (prob 1/5), 1 (prob 1/5), 2 (prob 1/5), 6 (prob 1/10), 9 (prob 1/10), 12 (prob 1/5).
game.contract: The contract settles at the largest of the dice.

info.raw:
Fair value is about **9.09** (the expected maximum of the three dice). I'm quoting 7.7 bid and 10.5 ask, roughly 1.4 either side of fair value.

**Expected maximum.** I used E[M] = Σ P(M > m) for m = 0 to 11. The table gives P(M ≤ m) = F1(m) · F2(m) · F3(m), where F1, F2 and F3 are the chances that dice 1, 2 and 3 are each at most m.

| m | F1 | F2 | F3 | P(M ≤ m) | P(M > m) |
|---|----|----|----|----------|----------|
| 0–3 | – | – | – | 0 (die 2 never shows below 4) | 1 |
| 4 | 0.5 | 0.25 | 0.6 | 0.075 | 0.925 |
| 5 | 0.5 | 0.25 | 0.6 | 0.075 | 0.925 |
| 6 | 0.5 | 0.5 | 0.7 | 0.175 | 0.825 |
| 7 | 0.5 | 0.75 | 0.7 | 0.2625 | 0.7375 |
| 8 | 1 | 0.75 | 0.7 | 0.525 | 0.475 |
| 9 | 1 | 0.75 | 0.8 | 0.6 | 0.4 |
| 10 | 1 | 0.75 | 0.8 | 0.6 | 0.4 |
| 11 | 1 | 0.75 | 0.8 | 0.6 | 0.4 |

Summing: E[M] = 4 + 0.925 + 0.925 + 0.825 + 0.7375 + 0.475 + 0.4 + 0.4 + 0.4 ≈ 9.09.

**Spread.** The settlement value is widely spread, so an informed trader would gain a lot against a tight quote. Noise traders' valuations vary with a standard deviation of 2.6. A half-spread of about 1.4 balances losses to informed traders against profit from noise traders.

{"bid": 7.7, "ask": 10.5}

Expected settlement (the largest of the three dice) is about **9.09**. Settlement equals 12 with probability 0.4, so any ask below 12 gets picked off by informed traders whenever the max is 12. Comparing expected profit per side against noise and informed flow puts the best ask near 11.5–11.7 and the best bid near 7.0.

**Max of dice 1 and 2:**
- 4 with probability 1/8
- 6 with probability 1/8
- 7 with probability 1/8
- 8 with probability 3/8
- 12 with probability 1/4
- The mean is 8.125.

**Adding die 3:**
- If die 3 shows 0, 1 or 2 (probability 0.6), the max stays 8.125 on average.
- If die 3 shows 6 (probability 0.1), the average max is 8.375.
- If die 3 shows 9 (probability 0.1), the average max is 9.75.
- If die 3 shows 12 (probability 0.2), the max is 12.
- Overall expected value is about 9.09.

**Ask side:** Below 12, informed buyers cost about 0.08 × (12 − ask). Noise buyers above the ask earn their margin over 9.09.
- Expected profit is about 0.21 at an ask of 10.5.
- It is about 0.27 at 11.0.
- It is about 0.30 at 11.5.
- The optimum is around 11.5–11.7.

**Bid side:** The settlement values below fair are 4, 6, 7 and 8.
- Expected profit is about 0.18 at a bid of 8.0.
- It is about 0.29 at 7.0.
- It is about 0.28 at 6.5.
- The optimum is near 7.0.

{"bid": 7.0, "ask": 11.6}

With die 3 = 1, the contract is just the larger of die 1 and die 2. Die 2 is always at least 4, so die 3 no longer matters.

**Settlement distribution (16 equally likely combinations)**

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 4 | 2/16 |
| 6 | 2/16 |
| 7 | 2/16 |
| 8 | 6/16 |
| 12 | 4/16 |

The fair value is 8.125.

**Ask side**
- An informed counterparty only buys from me when the value is 12.
- That costs 0.2 × 0.25 × (12 − ask) in expected value.
- I weigh this against the edge from noise traders, whose valuations are spread around 8.125 with SD 2.6.
- The best expected profit is about 0.27 per quote, at an ask of about 10.5.

**Bid side**
- An informed counterparty sells to me when the value is 4, 6 or 7.
- A counterparty valuing at exactly 6 does not sell, because it only sells below my bid.
- So a bid of 6.0 only loses to informed sellers when the value is 4.
- Expected profit is about 0.30 per quote at a bid of 6.0, the best of the levels I checked.

{"bid": 6.0, "ask": 10.5}

Die 3 = 1, so settlement is the larger of die 1 and die 2.

**Prior over the 16 equally likely combinations**

| Value | Count | Probability |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 2 | 2/16 |
| 6 | 2 | 2/16 |
| 7 | 2 | 2/16 |
| 8 | 6 | 6/16 |
| 12 | 4 | 4/16 |

The prior mean is 8.125.

**Update on the buy at 10.5**

- Only the outcome 12 is above 10.5, so an informed trader buys only if the value is 12.
- A noise trader buys if its valuation beats 10.5, which happens with probability P(N > 2.375/2.6) ≈ 0.18.
- If the value is 12, the chance of a buy is 0.2 + 0.8 × 0.18 ≈ 0.344.
- If the value is not 12, the chance of a buy is 0.8 × 0.18 ≈ 0.144.
- Updating gives P(12) ≈ 0.443.
- The other outcomes average 6.83, so the public fair value is about 0.443 × 12 + 0.557 × 6.83 ≈ **9.12**.

**Choosing the quotes**

- **Ask:** an informed buyer only loses me money if the value is 12. Asking 12 removes that loss entirely and still earns about 0.31 per quote from noise traders. That is the best ask I found.
- **Bid:** an informed seller hurts when the value is 4 or 6, and also 7 if I bid above 7. Expected profit peaks around 6.5–7, at roughly 0.28 per quote.
- I'll bid 6.6. Buying would also cover part of my short position.

{"bid": 6.6, "ask": 12.0}

Die 1 = 8 and die 3 = 1, so the result depends only on die 2:
- If die 2 shows 4, 6 or 7 (probability 3/4), the contract settles at 8.
- If die 2 shows 12 (probability 1/4), it settles at 12.

So the public fair value is 0.75 × 8 + 0.25 × 12 = 9.

**Ask side.** An informed trader buys only when the true value is 12 (probability 0.2 × 0.25 = 0.05 per quote), and only if my ask is below 12. Noise traders value the contract at 9 + N(0, 2.6).

Expected profit = 0.8 × P(noise buys) × (a − 9) − 0.05 × (12 − a).
- At a = 11.5: 0.8 × 0.168 × 2.5 − 0.025 ≈ 0.31.
- At a = 11.6: also about 0.31.
- At a = 12: about 0.30.
- At a = 11: about 0.30.

The best ask is about 11.5.

**Bid side.** An informed trader sells when the true value is 8 (probability 0.15), but only if my bid is above 8. A bid at or below 8 removes that loss. The remaining profit from noise traders is:
- At b = 8: about 0.28.
- At b = 7: about 0.35.
- At b = 6.5: about 0.34.

The best bid is about 7.

My position of −1 is well within limits, so I don't need to adjust for inventory.

{"bid": 7.0, "ask": 11.5}

The contract settles at the largest die. Die 1 = 8 and die 3 = 1 are revealed, so settlement is max(8, die 2):

- Die 2 is 4, 6 or 7 (probability 3/4): settles at 8.
- Die 2 is 12 (probability 1/4): settles at 12.

Fair value is therefore 0.75 × 8 + 0.25 × 12 = **9**.

**Ask:**
- An informed trader buys only when the value is 12, which happens with probability 0.2 × 0.25 = 0.05. Any ask below 12 loses (12 − ask) to that trader.
- A noise trader buys with probability 0.8 × P(valuation > ask), and I gain (ask − 9).
- Asks between 11.3 and 11.5 give an expected profit of about 0.31.
- 11.4 sits in that range.

**Bid:**
- If my bid is 8 or lower, an informed trader never sells to me, because the value is at least 8.
- A noise trader sells with probability 0.8 × P(valuation < bid), and I gain (9 − bid).
- A bid of 7 is about the best, at roughly 0.35 expected profit. 8 gives about 0.28 and 6.5 about 0.34.

My position of −1 allows trading on either side, so I quote both.

{"bid": 7, "ask": 11.4}

game.description:
Two dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 0, 2, 2, 3, 5, 5, 10.
- Die 2 (4 faces, loaded): 0 (prob 1/10), 3 (prob 3/10), 4 (prob 1/5), 5 (prob 2/5).
game.contract: The contract settles at the smallest of the dice.

info.raw:
I priced the contract from its probability distribution, then set each side of the quote to maximise expected edge against the mix of informed and noise traders.

**Fair value**

Die 1 is 0, 2, 3, 5 or 10 with probabilities 2/8, 2/8, 1/8, 2/8, 1/8. The expected minimum for each value of die 2:

| Die 2 | Probability | E[min] |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.1 | 0 |
| 3 | 0.3 | 2 |
| 4 | 0.2 | 2.375 |
| 5 | 0.4 | 2.75 |

Weighting these gives a fair value of 0.6 + 0.475 + 1.1 = **2.175**.

The distribution of the minimum is:
- 0 with probability 0.325
- 2 with probability 0.225
- 3 with probability 0.225
- 4 with probability 0.075
- 5 with probability 0.15

**Ask side**

- Informed traders only buy when the value is 4 or 5.
- An ask of about 4.0 gives the best expected edge, about +0.13 per quote.
- Noise traders (fair value plus noise with standard deviation 1.8) still reach that price often enough.
- Lower asks are bought by informed traders whenever the value is 3, which costs too much.

**Bid side**

- Informed traders sell whenever the value is below the bid, and a value of 0 has probability 0.325.
- A bid of about 0.1 is near-optimal, with expected edge of about +0.16.
- Higher bids hand too much to informed sellers holding a 0.

{"bid": 0.1, "ask": 4.0}

The fair value is about 2.2 after the no-trade at quote 1, so I'll quote bid 0.1 and ask 4.1.

**Prior distribution of the minimum:**

| Value | Probability |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0.325 |
| 2 | 0.225 |
| 3 | 0.1125 |
| 4 | 0.075 |
| 5 | 0.15 |

The prior mean is about 1.84.

**Update after quote 1 (bid 0.1, ask 4, no trade):**
- The noise trader centres on about 1.84, so it would not trade with probability about 0.72.
- If the value is 0, an informed trader would have sold at 0.1. If the value is 5, it would have bought at 4. Either way the chance of no trade is only about 0.47.
- For values 2, 3 or 4, the informed trader would not trade, so the chance of no trade is about 0.82.

The posterior is about 0: 0.27, 2: 0.33, 3: 0.16, 4: 0.11, 5: 0.125. The fair value is now about 2.2.

**Choosing the quotes:**
- **Ask:** Above 4, only a value of 5 loses money to an informed buyer. Noise traders above the ask still pay well. Expected profit is highest around 4.1, at about +0.14.
- **Bid:** Only a value of 0 loses to an informed seller. Expected profit is highest near 0.0–0.1, at about +0.15.

{"bid": 0.1, "ask": 4.1}

Die 2 is 5, so the contract settles at the smaller of die 1 and 5.

**Possible settlement values:**
- 0 with probability 1/4
- 2 with probability 1/4
- 3 with probability 1/8
- 5 with probability 3/8

The public fair value is (0+0+2+2+3+5+5+5)/8 = **2.75**.

**Ask side.** An informed buyer only hurts me when the value is 5, which happens with probability 3/8. Noise buyers pay me the ask minus 2.75. I estimated expected profit per quote at a few ask levels:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 4.5 | 0.12 |
| 4.8 | 0.14 |
| 4.9 | 0.15 |
| 5.0 | 0.15 |

The best is about **4.9**.

**Bid side.** An informed seller hurts me when the value is 0, which happens with probability 1/4. Expected profit at a few bid levels:

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 1.5 | 0.067 |
| 1.0 | 0.10 |
| 0.5 | 0.111 |
| 0.1 | 0.113 |
| 0.0 | 0.113 |

The curve is flat near zero, so I'll bid **0.1**.

{"bid": 0.1, "ask": 4.9}

The contract is now worth roughly 4.18, so I'll bid 2.3 and ask 5.6, which is about where each side's expected profit peaks.

**Settlement values.** Die 2 = 5, so the contract settles at min(die 1, 5). Over the eight equally likely die 1 faces that gives 0, 0, 2, 2, 3, 5, 5, 5, with a mean of 2.75.

**What the quote 3 trade tells us.** Someone bought at 4.9, which only pays off for an informed trader if the value is 5.
- If the value is 5, a buy is likely: 0.35 (informed) + 0.65 × P(noise > 4.9 | fair 2.75) ≈ 0.35 + 0.65 × 0.116 ≈ 0.426.
- If the value is anything else, only a noise trader buys: about 0.076.

Updating on that buy:
- P(value = 5) ≈ 0.77.
- Each of the values 0, 0, 2, 2, 3 has probability about 0.046.
- So the fair value is about 0.77 × 5 + 0.23 × 1.4 ≈ 4.18.

**Choosing the ask.** An ask at 5 or higher can never be hit by an informed trader, because the value cannot exceed 5. Only noise traders, centred on 4.18, can buy there. Expected profit from the ask:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 5.0 | 0.17 |
| 5.3 | 0.195 |
| 5.6 | 0.199 |
| 5.8 | 0.194 |

**Choosing the bid.** A higher bid catches more noise sellers but also lets informed traders sell when the value is 0 or 2. Expected profit from the bid:

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 2.0 | 0.096 |
| 2.3 | 0.098 |
| 2.5 | 0.096 |
| 2.9 | 0.077 |
| 3.5 | about −0.01 |

**Position.** I'm short 1, so either a buy or a sell keeps me within the ±3 limit.

{"bid": 2.3, "ask": 5.6}

game.title: Dice/cards min
game.description: A custom deck of 22 cards is shuffled: 2 cards worth 2, 3 cards worth 3, 4 cards worth 4, 4 cards worth 5, 2 cards worth 12, 4 cards worth 13, 3 cards worth 15. 3 cards are dealt face down, without replacement.
game.contract: The contract settles at the smallest of the dealt cards.

info.raw:
Expected minimum of 3 cards ≈ 3.77. My bid of 2.0 sits at the lowest card value, so an informed trader never sells to me at a loss. My ask of 5.5 sits above 5, so I only lose to informed buyers when the minimum is 12 or more, which has about a 5.5% chance. In both cases the expected profit from noise traders outweighs the informed losses.

{"bid": 2.0, "ask": 5.5}

Before any cards are revealed, the fair value is the expected minimum of 3 cards drawn from the 22-card deck. That is about **3.77**.

**Distribution of the minimum (out of C(22,3) = 1540 deals):**

| Minimum | Probability |
|---|---|
| 2 | 0.26 |
| 3 | 0.30 |
| 4 | 0.26 |
| 5 | 0.13 |
| 12 or more | 0.055 |

Most of the settlement value sits between 2 and 5. There is a small tail around 12–15, and that tail is the main risk of being lifted by an informed buyer. The no-trade on quote 1 tells us very little.

**Ask at 4.8**
- Noise traders buy about 33% of the time, earning about 1.03 each time.
- An informed buyer only lifts us when the minimum is 5 or higher. The expected loss from that is about 0.09.
- Net, this side has clearly positive expected value.

**Bid at 2.8**
- Noise traders sell about 34% of the time, earning about 0.97 each time.
- An informed seller only hits us when the minimum is 2. That loss is small, about 0.04.

{"bid": 2.8, "ask": 4.8}

Card 1 is a 4, so settlement is the smaller of 4 and the two unseen cards.

**Prior from the remaining 21 cards**
- P(settles at 2) = 39/210, because at least one 2 is among the two cards.
- P(settles at 3) = 51/210, because there is a 3 but no 2.
- P(settles at 4) = 120/210.

**Update from the stage-1 trade**
- A seller hit my bid at 2.8. An informed trader only does that if the settlement is below 2.8, which means it is 2.
- That makes the 2 outcome about 1.7 times more likely relative to the others.
- Posterior is roughly 2 → 0.28, 3 → 0.215, 4 → 0.51, giving a fair value of about 3.23.

**Choosing the quotes**
- **Ask:** An informed buyer only lifts my offer when the value is 4. Above 4 there is no adverse selection, but a noise buyer is still reasonably likely. I'm long one unit, so I'm happy to sell. An ask around 4.1 captures most of the noise edge.
- **Bid:** An informed seller only hits it when the value is 2. Being long, I want to bid low to avoid adding to my position. A bid around 2.3 keeps the loss to informed sellers small while still earning a decent edge from noise sellers.

{"bid": 2.3, "ask": 4.1}

Card 1 is a 4, so the settlement value is min(4, card 2, card 3). Fair value is about 3.39.

**Fair value.** Of the 21 cards left, 16 are worth 4 or more. There are two 2s and three 3s.
- P(settle = 4) = (16/21)(15/20) = 240/420 ≈ 0.571
- P(settle = 2) = 1 − (19/21)(18/20) = 78/420 ≈ 0.186
- P(settle = 3) = 102/420 ≈ 0.243
- Expected value = (2·78 + 3·102 + 4·240) / 420 ≈ **3.39**

**Informed traders.** The settlement can only be 2, 3 or 4.
- An ask of 4.0 or higher can never be lifted by an informed trader, because their valuation is at most 4.
- A bid of 2.0 or lower can never be hit by an informed trader, because their valuation is at least 2.
- So quoting outside [2, 4] means only noise traders trade with me.

**Noise traders.** Their valuations are centred at 3.39 with standard deviation 2.3. I chose each side to maximise expected profit per quote, which is 0.8 × fill probability × edge.
- Ask: 4.0 gives about 0.19, 4.6 about 0.29 and 5.0 about 0.31. The optimum is near 5.0–5.1.
- Bid: 2.5 gives about 0.23, 2.0 about 0.30 and 1.8 about 0.31. The optimum is near 1.9.

Being long 1 is well inside the position limits, so the position does not change the quotes.

{"bid": 1.9, "ask": 5.0}

Card 1 and card 2 are both 4, so the settlement value is min(4, card 3).

**Fair value.** The 20 remaining cards are: two 2s, three 3s, two 4s, four 5s, two 12s, four 13s and three 15s.
- P(value = 2) = 2/20
- P(value = 3) = 3/20
- P(value = 4) = 15/20

Fair value = 0.2 + 0.45 + 3.0 = **3.65**.

The value can only be 2, 3 or 4. So an ask at 4 or above can never be lifted by an informed trader. A bid at 2.0 or below can never be hit by one either, because a seller needs a valuation strictly below the bid.

**Ask side.** I estimated the expected edge from noise buyers, with noise standard deviation 2.3:

| Ask | Expected edge |
|---|---|
| 4.5 | 0.24 |
| 5.0 | 0.30 |
| 5.5 | 0.31 |
| 6.0 | 0.29 |

The best ask is about 5.4.

**Bid side.** The expected edge peaks at about 0.31, for a bid between 1.9 and 2.0. With no informed risk there and a very flat curve, either works.

**Position.** I am long 2. One more buy takes me to the +3 cap, which would only remove my bid on the last quote, so the cost is small.

I'll bid 1.9 and ask 5.4.

{"bid": 1.9, "ask": 5.4}

Only the third card is still hidden. That leaves 20 cards: two 2s, three 3s, two 4s, four 5s, two 12s, four 13s and three 15s.

The contract settles at min(4, card 3):
- It settles at 2 with probability 2/20 = 0.10.
- It settles at 3 with probability 3/20 = 0.15.
- It settles at 4 with probability 15/20 = 0.75.

Fair value is 0.2 + 0.45 + 3.0 = **3.65**.

The settlement value is at most 4. With an ask at 4 or above, an informed trader never buys from me. With a bid at 2 or below, an informed trader never sells to me. So only noise traders can trade with me, and their valuations are centred on 3.65 with standard deviation 2.3.

The expected profit on each side is x·P(noise > 3.65 + x), where x is the distance from fair value. This is largest at about x ≈ 0.75σ ≈ 1.7. That gives an ask near 5.4 and a bid near 1.9. Both levels are clear of any informed trading. My position is +2, so one more buy is still allowed.

{"bid": 1.9, "ask": 5.4}

game.title: Dice/cards max
game.description: A custom deck of 20 cards is shuffled: 3 cards worth 3, 1 card worth 4, 1 card worth 5, 4 cards worth 7, 2 cards worth 9, 3 cards worth 10, 3 cards worth 11, 3 cards worth 15. 3 cards are dealt face down, without replacement.
game.contract: The contract settles at the largest of the dealt cards.

info.raw:
Fair value is about 11.98, so I quote 9.8 / 14.3: wide on both sides, a little asymmetric because informed buying is the bigger risk.

**Fair value.** I worked out the expected maximum of 3 cards drawn from the 20 by counting how many 3-card hands have every card at or below each value (out of 1,140 hands):

| Max card | Probability |
|---|---|
| 15 | 0.40 |
| 11 | 0.28 |
| 10 | 0.17 |
| 9 | 0.07 |
| 7 | 0.065 |
| 3, 4 or 5 | about 0.01 |

E[max] = 13,658 / 1,140 ≈ 11.98.

**Ask.** The main risk on the ask is an informed buyer when the true value is 15, which happens with probability 0.2 × 0.4. Weighing noise-trader profit against that informed loss:
- At an ask of 13.5, expected profit per quote is about 0.23.
- At 14.0 it is about 0.29.
- At 14.5 it is about 0.31, the best of these.
- At 15.0 it is about 0.32 in the noise-only figure, but that leaves out the informed side.

**Bid.** On the bid, the informed loss is smaller because of the downside tail. Expected profit per quote is about 0.31 at both 9.5 and 10.0, and drops to 0.25 at 10.5.

Since 9.5 and 10.0 come out the same on the bid, I set it at 9.8. On the ask, 14.5 scored best, but I shade it down to 14.3.

{"bid": 9.8, "ask": 14.3}

The public fair value is now about 13.0, so I'm quoting 11.4 bid / 14.6 ask.

**Prior expected value of the maximum card.** I counted how many cards are worth each value or less, out of 1140 possible 3-card hands:

| Max value | Probability |
|---|---|
| 3 | 1/1140 |
| 4 | 3/1140 |
| 5 | 6/1140 |
| 7 | 74/1140 |
| 9 | 81/1140 |
| 10 | 199/1140 |
| 11 | 316/1140 |
| 15 | 460/1140 |

This gives an expected value of about 11.98. The chance that a 15 was dealt is about 40%.

**Update on the buy at 14.3.** A buy at 14.3 only makes sense for an informed trader if the value is 15.
- A noise trader buys if their valuation exceeds 14.3, which happens about 20% of the time.
- If the value is 15, a buy happens with probability 0.2 + 0.8 × 0.198 ≈ 0.358.
- If the value is not 15, a buy happens with probability about 0.158.
- So the chance of a 15 rises to about 0.61.
- If the value is not 15, its expected value is about 9.94.
- The updated fair value is 0.606 × 15 + 0.394 × 9.94 ≈ 13.0.

**Choosing the quote.**
- **Ask at 14.6:** An informed buyer only arrives if the value is 15, and then I lose just 0.4. Noise buyers pay me about 1.6 above fair value. The expected edge is positive, about +0.3.
- **Bid at 11.4:** An informed seller arrives when the value is 11 or less, which averages about 9.9. Noise sellers give me about 1.6 of edge. The expected edge is again positive, about +0.2.

I'm short 1, so I lean the bid up slightly.

{"bid": 11.4, "ask": 14.6}

Fair value is about 13.7, mainly because two buys at 14.3 and 14.6 make it likely a 15 was dealt.

**Prior:** The expected maximum of 3 cards from the deck is about 11.98. The chance the maximum is 15 is 460/1140 ≈ 0.40.

**Updating on the trades:**
- After the buy at 14.3:
  - If the max is 15, the buy is about 2.3 times as likely, since an informed trader always buys and noise traders buy about 16% of the time.
  - P(max = 15) rises to about 0.60, and fair value to about 13.0.
- After the buy at 14.6:
  - The same update with a likelihood ratio of about 1.9.
  - P(max = 15) rises to about 0.74.
  - If the max is not 15, its expected value is about 9.94.
  - Fair value is therefore about 0.74 × 15 + 0.26 × 9.94 ≈ 13.7.

**Quote:**
- **Ask 15.1:** This is above the highest possible settlement of 15, so any sale is guaranteed profit and informed traders will never buy. Noise traders still buy about 30% of the time. The only cost is reaching the -3 position limit.
- **Bid 12.6:** I am short 2, so I set the bid a bit closer to fair value to encourage covering. It stays far enough below 13.7 to limit losses to informed sellers, who sell only when the max is not 15.

{"bid": 12.6, "ask": 15.1}

Card 1 is a 15, which is the highest card in the deck. So the settlement value is certain to be **15**, and the public fair value is 15.

- **Informed traders:** they value the contract at exactly 15. With my bid below 15 and my ask above 15, they never trade with me.
- **Noise traders:** their valuation is 15 plus Normal noise with standard deviation 2.7.
- **Choosing the spread:** on each side, my expected profit is the edge (x) times the chance a noise trader crosses. That is x·Φ(−x/2.7), which is largest at about x ≈ 0.75 × 2.7 ≈ 2.
- **Position:** I am short 2, so I can buy up to 5 more units and sell 1 more. Both sides are allowed and both have positive expected value.

So I quote 2 below and 2 above the fair value of 15.

{"bid": 13.0, "ask": 17.0}

Card 1 is 15, the highest card in the deck, so the contract will settle at exactly 15. That is also the public fair value.

- **Informed traders:** they value the contract at exactly 15. They will not trade at a bid below 15 or an ask above 15.
- **Noise traders:** they value it at 15 + N(0, 2.7).
  - Expected profit per side at distance d from 15 is roughly 0.8 · d · Φ(−d/2.7).
  - This peaks near d ≈ 2: about 0.46 per side at d = 2, versus 0.43 at d = 1.5 and 0.44 at d = 2.5.
  - So I quote 13 / 17.
- **Position:** I'm short 2. A fill on either side keeps me within limits (−3 or −1).

{"bid": 13.0, "ask": 17.0}

Card 1 is a 15, which is the highest card in the deck, so the contract settles at exactly 15. The fair value is now known with certainty, and informed traders no longer give anyone an edge against me.

**Where to quote:** Noise traders value the contract at 15 plus Normal noise with standard deviation 2.7. On each side I want the spread x from 15 that maximises x·(1 − Φ(x/2.7)). That peaks around x ≈ 0.75 × 2.7 ≈ 2.0. So the best quotes are a bid of 13.0 and an ask of 17.0.

**Position:** Being short 2 carries no risk now that the settlement value is certain. Being pushed to -3 would only remove my ask on later quotes. So I keep the quotes symmetric.

{"bid": 13.0, "ask": 17.0}

Card 1 is a 15, which is the highest card in the deck, so the contract will settle at exactly **15**. There is no remaining uncertainty.

- **Informed traders** value the contract at 15. They will not trade with me as long as my bid is below 15 and my ask is above 15.
- **Noise traders** value it at 15 plus Normal noise with standard deviation 2.7. On each side, my expected profit is the edge times the chance they trade, or e·P(Z > e/2.7).
- **Best edge:** that product peaks at an edge of about 2. It gives about 0.46 per side, scaled by the 0.8 chance the counterparty is a noise trader.
- **Position:** I am at -2, so I can still sell one more unit (reaching -3) or buy back. Both sides stay open.

I will quote 2 below and 2 above the settlement value.

{"bid": 13.0, "ask": 17.0}

Card 1 is a 15, the highest card in the deck, so the contract will settle at exactly 15. No risk is left in the price.

- **Informed traders** value the contract at exactly 15. They will never cross a quote that sits away from 15.
- **Noise traders** value it at 15 plus Normal noise with standard deviation 2.7.
- **Best spread:** profit per side is the edge times the chance a trader crosses it. That is highest when each side is about 0.75 standard deviations from 15, which is roughly 2.0.
- **Position:** I am short 2, so I can still sell one more unit before hitting the limit of -3. Buying back also locks in a profit.

So I quote 13 and 17, with 2.0 of edge on each side.

{"bid": 13.0, "ask": 17.0}

Card 1 is 15, the highest card in the deck, so the contract settles at exactly 15.

- **Informed traders:** they value the contract at exactly 15. They won't trade if my bid is below 15 and my ask is above 15.
- **Noise traders:** they value it at 15 plus noise with standard deviation 2.7. My expected profit on each side is the half-spread s times the chance their noise exceeds s. That is largest at about s = 0.75 × 2.7 ≈ 2.0.
- **Position:** I am at -2, so I can still sell one unit (to -3) or buy one unit.

I'll quote 2.0 either side of 15.

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 1/2, P(heads) = 1 with probability 1/2. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 6 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
Before any reveals, the settlement value is either:
- 6 heads for sure, if the coin always lands heads (probability 1/2), or
- a Binomial(6, 0.5) count, if the coin is fair (probability 1/2).

That gives an expected value of 0.5·3 + 0.5·6 = **4.5**. The value is 6 with probability about 0.508. Below 6, the probabilities fall off with the binomial shape.

**Ask side.** An informed trader buys at my ask only if the true value is above it. Since the value can't exceed 6, an ask of 6 or higher carries no informed risk. The trade-off is that a higher ask means fewer noise buyers but a larger margin on each.
- Ask 6.0 gives an expected profit of about 0.34.
- Ask 6.5 gives about 0.35.
- Ask 7.0 gives about 0.34.

**Bid side.** An informed trader sells at my bid only if the true value is below it, so low outcomes cost me money.
- Bid 3.0 gives an expected profit of about 0.29.
- Bid 2.5 gives about 0.32.
- Bid 2.0 gives about 0.33.

These are nearly flat, so I'll take 2.5 and keep the quote somewhat more balanced.

{"bid": 2.5, "ask": 6.5}

Repeat the 2.5 / 6.5 quote: both sides are near their expected-profit optimum.

**Fair value.** Half the time the coin is fair, so heads over 6 flips follow a binomial(6, 0.5) with mean 3. Half the time the coin always lands heads, giving 6. The fair value is 0.5 × 3 + 0.5 × 6 = 4.5. Last quote's no-trade tells us almost nothing, so it stays near 4.5.

**Ask side.** An informed trader holding the always-heads coin values the contract at 6. It buys if my ask is below 6. Expected profit per quote:
- Ask 5.5: about 0.23.
- Ask 6.0: about 0.34.
- Ask 6.5: about 0.35, the best of the three.
- Ask 7.0: about 0.34.

**Bid side.** Informed sellers hold low settlement values from the fair coin. Expected profit per quote:
- Bid 3.5: about 0.20.
- Bid 3.0: about 0.29.
- Bid 2.5: about 0.32.
- Bid 2.0: about 0.32.

{"bid": 2.5, "ask": 6.5}

The bid of 3.5 and ask of 7.5 both come from maximising expected profit per side.

**Probabilities after two heads**
- Chance the coin is the always-heads coin: 0.5 / (0.5 + 0.125) = 0.8.
- Chance the coin is fair: 0.2.

**Settlement distribution**
- Settlement is 2 plus the heads in the 4 remaining flips.
- If the coin is always-heads, settlement is 6.
- If the coin is fair, settlement is 2 + Bin(4, 0.5).
- So P(6) = 0.8125, P(5) = 0.05, P(4) = 0.075, P(3) = 0.05, P(2) = 0.0125.
- Public fair value = 0.8 × 6 + 0.2 × 4 = 5.6.

**Ask side**
- An informed trader buys only if the value is strictly above my ask.
- So any ask of 6 or more takes no informed buys; only noise traders buy there.
- Expected profit per arrival is 0.8 × P(noise valuation > ask) × (ask − 5.6):

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 6.0 | 0.14 |
| 7.0 | 0.33 |
| 7.5 | 0.354 (highest) |
| 8.0 | 0.34 |

**Bid side**
- An informed trader sells only if the value is below my bid, which costs me a little on the low outcomes.
- Expected profit per arrival, net of that cost:

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 3.0 | 0.33 |
| 3.5 | 0.343 (highest) |
| 4.0 | 0.33 |
| 4.5 | 0.27 |

{"bid": 3.5, "ask": 7.5}

Two heads make the always-heads coin much more likely, so I quote about 2 below and 1.9 above fair value: **bid 3.5, ask 7.5**.

**Which coin is it?** We started at even odds between the two coins.
- The chance of two heads is 1/4 for the fair coin and 1 for the always-heads coin.
- So P(always-heads coin) = 1 / (1 + 1/4) = 0.8, and P(fair coin) = 0.2.

**Settlement value:** it is 2 plus the heads in flips 3–6.
- With the always-heads coin it is 6.
- With the fair coin it is 2 plus a Binomial(4, 0.5), which averages 4.
- Fair value = 0.8 × 6 + 0.2 × 4 = **5.6**.

The buy at 7.5 tells us nothing. Settlement can be at most 6, so an informed trader would never pay 7.5. That trade must have come from a noise trader.

**Ask side:**
- An ask of 6 or higher means an informed trader never buys, because the value cannot exceed 6.
- Expected profit from noise buyers is 0.8 × P(5.6 + N(0, 2.6) > a) × (a − 5.6).
- This peaks near a = 7.5, at about 0.35 per quote.

**Bid side:**
- An informed trader sells only when the value is below the bid. Values of 2 and 3 are rare, with probabilities 0.0125 and 0.05.
- Expected profit from noise sellers peaks near 3.5, also about 0.35 per quote.
- The loss from informed sellers at that bid is only about 0.01.

**Position:** we are at −1, so there is plenty of room on both sides with 3 quotes left.

{"bid": 3.5, "ask": 7.5}

The coin is almost certainly the always-heads coin. Fair value is about 5.94, and I quote 4.0 / 8.0 so informed traders cannot profit from me and noise traders pay a wide spread.

**Fair value**
- After four heads, P(always-heads coin) = (1/2 × 1) / (1/2 × 1 + 1/2 × 1/16) = 16/17.
- If it is the always-heads coin, the last two flips add 2 heads. If it is the fair coin, they add 1 on average.
- So E[settlement] = 4 + (16/17)·2 + (1/17)·1 ≈ **5.94**.

**Settlement distribution**
- Value 6 with probability ≈ 0.956.
- Value 5 with probability ≈ 0.029.
- Value 4 with probability ≈ 0.015.

**What the earlier trade tells me**
- Someone bought at 7.5 in quote 3, but settlement can never exceed 6.
- An informed trader would never pay 7.5, so that buyer was a noise trader. The trade carries no information.

**Ask side**
- An informed trader values the contract at 6 at most. Any ask of 6 or more means they never buy.
- Only noise traders buy. Their valuation is about 5.94 plus noise with standard deviation 2.6.
- Expected profit per quote from the ask, by ask level:

| Ask | Chance a noise trader buys | Edge per trade | Expected profit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7.0 | 0.34 | 1.06 | 0.36 |
| 7.5 | 0.27 | 1.56 | 0.43 |
| 8.0 | 0.215 | 2.06 | 0.44 |
| 8.5 | 0.16 | 2.56 | 0.42 |

- The best ask is about **8.0**.

**Bid side**
- An informed trader only sells if their valuation is below my bid. The lowest possible value is 4, so a bid of 4.0 never trades with them.
- At 4.0, the chance a noise trader sells is about 0.23, at an edge of 1.94. That is roughly 0.44 per quote.
- Raising the bid to 4.5 or lowering it to 3.5 gives slightly less (about 0.42).

My position is -1, well within the ±4 limit, so I can quote both sides.

{"bid": 4.0, "ask": 8.0}

**Fair value:** about 5.94.
- After four straight heads, the chance the coin is the always-heads one is (1/2) / (1/2 + 1/2 · 1/16) = 16/17.
- If it is always-heads, the contract settles at 6. If it is fair, the two remaining flips add 0, 1 or 2 heads, so settlement is 4, 5 or 6 with probabilities 1/4, 1/2, 1/4.
- Combining these gives settlement 6 with probability about 0.956, 5 with about 0.029, and 4 with about 0.015. The expected value is 101/17 ≈ 5.94.

**Ask:** 7.5.
- Any ask of 6 or more avoids the informed trader in almost every case, because its valuation is at most 6.
- Against noise traders (standard deviation 2.6), the best edge is about 0.61 standard deviations, or roughly 1.6, above fair value. That puts the ask at about 7.5.

**Bid:** 4.3.
- By the same logic, the bid goes about 1.6 below fair value, at about 4.3.
- The informed trader only sells into that bid if the settlement is 4, which has probability about 1/68, and the loss would be only 0.3. That cost is negligible.

**Position:** Since only expected profit matters and this is the last quote, my -1 position does not change the quote.

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 1/2, P(heads) = 1 with probability 1/2. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 6 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.

info.raw:
Bid 2.9, ask 6.0: both sides were chosen to maximise expected profit against the mix of informed and noise traders.

**Fair value.** Half the time the coin is fair, giving an expected 3 heads. Half the time it is double-headed, giving 6 heads. So the fair value is 0.5 × 3 + 0.5 × 6 = 4.5.

**What the informed trader knows.**
- About 50.8% of the time the settlement is exactly 6. That is the double-headed coin, plus the 1/64 chance of 6 heads from the fair coin.
- Otherwise the settlement follows a Binomial(6, 0.5), mostly between 1 and 5.

**Ask side.**
- The settlement can never exceed 6, so an ask at 6.0 can never lose to an informed buyer.
- Asks below 6 are hit by the informed trader about 51% of the time, and they lose up to (6 − ask) each time.
- I compared expected profit (noise-trader gain minus informed-trader loss) at several asks:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 5.5 | +0.09 |
| 5.8 | +0.15 |
| 6.0 | +0.18 |
| 6.1 | +0.18 |

- Profit is flat at the top, so I quote 6.0, the lowest ask with no informed-trader loss.

**Bid side.**
- An informed trader sells to me only when the settlement is below my bid, which happens only in the low tail of the fair coin.
- I compared expected profit at several bids:

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 2.5 | +0.104 |
| 2.8 | +0.105 |
| 3.0 | +0.102 |
| 3.5 | +0.04 |

- The best bids are around 2.8 to 3.0, so I quote 2.9.

{"bid": 2.9, "ask": 6.0}

**Ask side.** The settlement is exactly 6 with probability about 0.51. Any ask below 6 sells to every informed trader in that case, at a loss. At 5.9 that informed loss is about 0.02, which roughly cancels the extra noise-trader fills. An ask of 6.0 has no informed loss and earns about 0.19 per quote from noise buyers.

**Bid side.** Informed traders sell whenever the value is below my bid.

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 3.0 | about +0.10 |
| 2.5 | about +0.10 |
| 3.5 | about +0.05 (the 3-heads case gets picked off) |

So a bid near 3.0 is best.

{"bid": 3.0, "ask": 6.0}

The prior fair value is 4.5: half the time the coin is fair, giving an expected 3 heads, and half the time it is two-headed, giving 6. That value hasn't moved, since there have been no trades so far. Settlement is 6 with probability about 0.508, so an informed buyer is a real threat on the ask side.

**Ask:**
- At 5.9, an informed trader holding value 6 buys and costs me only 0.1.

**Bid:**

- An informed trader sells only when the coin is fair and shows 2 or fewer heads (probability about 0.17). Those cases average about 1.6, so each costs me about 1.4.

| Ask | Noise gain | Informed loss | Net expected profit |
|---|---|---|---|

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.3 with probability 2/5, P(heads) = 0.4 with probability 1/10, P(heads) = 0.9 with probability 1/2. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 8 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at 10 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
The contract's fair value is 48.8, but this game punishes tight quotes, so I'm quoting wide: bid 21, ask 77.

**Fair value.** The expected chance of heads is 0.4·0.3 + 0.1·0.4 + 0.5·0.9 = 0.61. Over 8 flips at 10 per head, the fair value is 80 × 0.61 = 48.8.

**Why the spread is wide.** The settlement value has two humps:
- If the 0.9 coin was picked (probability 0.5), the value clusters around 60–80. It is 80 with about 43% chance and 70 with about 38%.
- If one of the low coins was picked (probability 0.5), it clusters around 0–40.

So an informed trader almost always knows the value is far from 48.8. A tight quote would lose about 23 to them on roughly half of all informed arrivals.

**Choosing each side.** For each candidate quote I compared the expected profit from noise traders with the expected loss to informed traders.

| Side | Quote | Noise gain | Informed loss | Net per quote |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ask | 72 | ~2.81 | ~0.60 | ~2.2 |
| Ask | 75 | | | ~2.3 |
| Ask | 78 | ~2.49 | ~0.15 | ~2.34 |
| Ask | 80 | | | ~2.33 |
| Bid | 22 | | | ~2.07 |
| Bid | 25 | | | ~1.86 |
| Bid | 20 | | | ~2.03 |

On the ask side, 77–78 gives the best net. On the bid side, the best is around 21–22.

{"bid": 21, "ask": 77}

Fair value is about 32. Before any trade it was 48.8, and the sale at my bid of 21 pulls the estimate down toward the low-bias coins.

**Starting value.** The expected heads probability is 0.4·0.3 + 0.1·0.4 + 0.5·0.9 = 0.61. That gives an expected settlement of 80 × 0.61 = 48.8.

**Updating on the sale at 21.**
- An informed trader sells at 21 only if settlement is 20 or less, i.e. 2 or fewer heads. That has a prior probability of about 0.25.
- A noise trader sells if its valuation falls below 21. Its valuation is centred on 48.8 with sd 26, so that probability is about 0.14.
- Weighting each case by its likelihood, the posterior expected settlement is about 32.
- The posterior is bimodal. About 62% of the weight is on 0–2 heads, and about 21% is on 7–8 heads.

**Choosing the quotes.**
- **Bid:** A bid of 10 is only hit by an informed trader when there are 0 heads, which has about 6% probability, so adverse selection is small. A noise trader still sells about 20% of the time. Expected edge is about +2.6, which is the best of the bids I checked.
- **Ask:** Asks in the low 60s balance the risk of informed buyers on 7–8 heads against noise-trader flow. Expected edge is about +1.4 to +1.5.

{"bid": 10, "ask": 62}

Fair value is about 60.6. I'm quoting bid 39 and ask 76.

**Fair value**
- Each coin's likelihood of 3 heads in 4 flips is p³(1−p).
- The posterior coin probabilities are 0.158 for p = 0.3, 0.080 for p = 0.4 and 0.762 for p = 0.9.
- That gives E[p] ≈ 0.765.
- Expected heads are 3 revealed plus 4 × 0.765 for the remaining flips, about 6.06. Fair value ≈ 60.6.
- The two stage-1 sells (at 21 and 10) were not informed trades. An informed trader sells only if the value is below the bid, which needs at most 2 heads, and 3 heads are already revealed. So the history adds no information.

**Settlement distribution**

| Value | Probability |
|---|---|
| 70 | 0.503 |
| 60 | 0.246 |
| 50 | 0.107 |
| 40 | 0.096 |
| 30 | 0.048 |

- **Ask:** at 70 or above, informed traders never buy, so noise-trader profit dominates. Expected profit per quote rises to a peak of about 2.9 around an ask of 80. I shade it to 76 because I'm long 2 and want sells to cut inventory.
- **Bid:** above 40, informed sellers become costly (at a bid of 59 the expected profit is negative). Near 40 they only sell when the value is 30. Expected profit is about 2.7 at a bid of 40, and I shade it slightly to 39 for inventory.

| p | prior | likelihood × prior | posterior |

| Settlement | 70 | 60 | 50 | 40 | 30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.503 | 0.246 | 0.107 | 0.096 | 0.048 |

**Ask**

- An informed trader buys only if the settlement value is above the ask. At an ask of 70 or higher, informed traders never buy from me.
- So the ask only needs to make money against noise traders. Expected profit is 0.65 × (a − 60.6) × P(Z > (a − 60.6)/26).
- This peaks around 80, at about 2.9 per quote.

**Bid**

| Bid | Expected loss to informed | Expected gain from noise | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | −0.67 | +2.35 | 1.68 |
| 45 | −0.42 | +2.78 | 2.36 |
| 40 | −0.17 | +2.87 | ≈2.70 |
| 38 | −0.14 | +2.82 | 2.68 |

At a bid of 40, informed traders sell only when settlement is 30. The bid is best around 40.

My position of +2 leaves room to buy, since the limit is +5.
